text:
J.T. Compher is Detroit's do-a-bit-of-everything center, and right now the "everything" includes a lot of time in his own end. He has 3 goals and 7 points in 14 games on about 15 and a half minutes a night, which is roughly the pace you'd expect from him. The worry is the possession: with him on the ice at five on five, Detroit gets about 46% of the expected goals, the share of chance quality, and the team is almost six points better with him on the bench.

He was one of the voices after the 4-1 lead that turned into a 5-4 loss in Florida on Nov. 12, a night he scored on a breakaway. That loss sat in the middle of a stretch of six losses in seven games.

What he still does well: carry the puck in rather than dump it (54% of his entries, by Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking) and draw penalties, worth two goals on his own last season by Evolving-Hockey's count. A 2022 Cup winner from Colorado, he's being asked to steady a team that has wobbled.
